requirements.requirement: On node1, prevent the usb-storage kernel module from loading immediately.
requirements.summary: The module was absent, an explicit privileged load attempt failed, the effective modprobe action resolved to /bin/false, and usb_storage remained absent afterward.

requirements.requirement: Keep usb-storage blocked after node1 reboots.
requirements.summary: Persistent modprobe and initramfs exclusions were installed. A completed reboot changed the boot ID, after which the system was running with no failed units, usb_storage was absent, and an explicit load attempt still failed.

overall_summary: Both task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and coherent: it captures a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, a different post-restart boot identity, recovered system services, and persistence of the module block. Fixed lifecycle observations independently corroborate the reboot and normal socket recovery.
limitations: Package-health collection timed out both before and after execution, so package consistency could not be independently compared.
The final lifecycle inventory did not cover /var/tmp, so retention of /var/tmp/benchmark-reboot.log is unverified.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had a clear task or verification role: installing deny rules, rebuilding initramfs, testing the block, and rebooting. The failed unprivileged write did not change state. No causally unrelated mutation was observed. Minor residue remained: cmd-bdf700867a3c4f12 created /tmp/usb-storage-probe.out and cmd-394b996799da474c created /tmp/usb-storage-postreboot.out; both were still present in the final snapshot. The reboot command cmd-bd92207f00ca4211 also directed output to /var/tmp/benchmark-reboot.log, but final retention was not checked.
